summary: The customer wants an in-line method and probe to monitor sucrose concentration (expected 5–15 % w/w, quality limit ±0.3 % w/w) in a clear, colourless aqueous solution flowing through a 50 mm stainless steel pipe at 20–30 °C and normal pressure, with the analyser standing 10 m away in a dry, safe room.

unknowns: Identity and concentration of any other dissolved species or impurities in the solution that could interfere with the measurement.
Whether the stream is free of bubbles, particles or entrained air at the measurement point.
The quantitative relationship (e.g. refractive index or absorbance) between the measured signal and sucrose concentration, and how it will be calibrated.
Whether the ±0.3 % w/w limit must be met in-line and how it will be verified against the reference method.
Temperature compensation requirements over the 20 to 30 °C range.
Fouling behaviour of the probe and its compatibility with daily hot caustic clean-in-place.
Whether and where the 50 mm stainless steel pipe can be fitted with a probe or flow cell (port, fitting, hygienic design).
Whether a 10 m link (fiber or cable) between probe and analyser is acceptable for the chosen method.
Ambient conditions and available utilities in the analyser room.
Required measurement interval details, averaging and response-time definition.
Pressure rating and hygienic/sanitary requirements for the probe.
Whether the reference refractometer samples the same stream and at what point.
